lines.text: Checkpoint B, the last stop. Let's review Phases 4 and 5: charts, scalping and risk.
lines.say: Checkpoint B, the last stop. Let's review Phases four and five: charts, scalping and risk.

lines.text: Eight questions on T14 to T23: chart reading, risk maths and demo decisions.
lines.say: Eight questions on T fourteen to T twenty-three: chart reading, risk maths and demo decisions.

lines.text: Read each question, pick an answer, and pause the video whenever you need more time.
lines.say: Read each question, pick an answer, and pause the video whenever you need more time.

lines.text: Not graded here. The graded Checkpoint B quiz is in the interactive course.
lines.say: Not graded here. The graded Checkpoint B quiz is in the interactive course.

lines.text: Question one, from T14. Open 60,000, high 60,300, low 59,800, close 60,200. Which is true?
lines.say: Question one, from T fourteen. Open sixty thousand, high sixty thousand three hundred, low fifty-nine thousand eight hundred, close sixty thousand two hundred. Which is true?

lines.text: A. It's a green, up candle, and the top of its body is the close: 60,200.
lines.say: A. It's a green, up candle, and the top of its body is the close: sixty thousand two hundred.

lines.text: B mixes up high and close. 60,300 is the top of the wick, the highest price traded.
lines.say: B mixes up high and close. Sixty thousand three hundred is the top of the wick, the highest price traded.

lines.text: Question two, from T15. Five 1-minute candles become one 5-minute candle. What are its prices?
lines.say: Question two, from T fifteen. Five one-minute candles become one five-minute candle. What are its prices?

lines.text: A. The first open, the highest high, the lowest low, and the last close.
lines.say: A. The first open, the highest high, the lowest low, and the last close.

lines.text: B is tempting, but candles don't average. They keep the real open, high, low and close.
lines.say: B is tempting, but candles don't average. They keep the real open, high, low and close.

lines.text: Question three, from T17. Price breaks above resistance, then falls back below within two candles.
lines.say: Question three, from T seventeen. Price breaks above resistance, then falls back below within two candles.

lines.text: B. It may be a fakeout. Wait for more evidence. No pattern is certain.
lines.say: B. It may be a fakeout. Wait for more evidence. No pattern is certain.

lines.text: A is the trap. A break alone is not confirmation, and buying on hope is not a plan.
lines.say: A is the trap. A break alone is not confirmation, and buying on hope is not a plan.

lines.text: Question four, from T18. A big green candle has very high volume. What can you conclude?
lines.say: Question four, from T eighteen. A big green candle has very high volume. What can you conclude?

lines.text: B. A lot was traded. That's one clue, not proof of where price goes next.
lines.say: B. A lot was traded. That's one clue, not proof of where price goes next.

lines.text: A is tempting, but volume alone never tells you the direction.
lines.say: A is tempting, but volume alone never tells you the direction.

lines.text: Question five, from T19. Each scalp makes +0.80 USDT gross, and fees cost 1.00. After 10 trades?
lines.say: Question five, from T nineteen. Each scalp makes plus zero point eight U-S-D-T gross, and fees cost one. After ten trades?

lines.text: B, minus 2.00 USDT. Each trade nets minus 0.20, and 10 times minus 0.20 is minus 2.00.
lines.say: B, minus two U-S-D-T. Each trade nets minus zero point two, and ten times minus zero point two is minus two.

lines.text: A forgets the fees. Many small trades mean many fees.
lines.say: A forgets the fees. Many small trades mean many fees.

lines.text: Question six, from T20 and T21. Mid-range, flat trend, low volume, no level near. Your decision?
lines.say: Question six, from T twenty and T twenty-one. Mid-range, flat trend, low volume, no level near. Your decision?

lines.text: C, NO_TRADE. Nothing lines up, so waiting is the sensible decision.
lines.say: C, no trade. Nothing lines up, so waiting is the sensible decision.

lines.text: A is the trap: one green candle is not a reason to take a risk.
lines.say: A is the trap: one green candle is not a reason to take a risk.

lines.text: Question seven, from T22. Risk budget 10 USDT. Stop 2% from entry. About what notional?
lines.say: Question seven, from T twenty-two. Risk budget ten U-S-D-T. Stop two percent from entry. About what notional?

lines.text: A, about 500 USDT. 10 divided by 2% is 500.
lines.say: A, about five hundred U-S-D-T. Ten divided by two percent is five hundred.

lines.text: B uses the whole account. 1,000 times 2% risks 20 USDT, double the budget.
lines.say: B uses the whole account. One thousand times two percent risks twenty U-S-D-T, double the budget.

lines.text: Question eight, from T23. Your demo stop slipped: minus 6.30 instead of minus 6. What next?
lines.say: Question eight, from T twenty-three. Your demo stop slipped: minus six point three instead of minus six. What next?

lines.text: B. Journal it, check the process, and take a break. A small slip is normal.
lines.say: B. Journal it, check the process, and take a break. A small slip is normal.

lines.text: A is revenge trading. Doubling the size doubles the risk.
lines.say: A is revenge trading. Doubling the size doubles the risk.

lines.text: Before you finish: critical safety.
lines.say: Before you finish: critical safety.

lines.text: Leverage magnifies losses. No leverage is safe, and liquidation can take your margin.
lines.say: Leverage magnifies losses. No leverage is safe, and liquidation can take your margin.

lines.text: A stop-loss is a trigger, not a promise. Gaps and slippage happen.
lines.say: A stop-loss is a trigger, not a promise. Gaps and slippage happen.

lines.text: Never share passwords, OTP or 2FA codes, or API secret keys. Not even with 'support'.
lines.say: Never share passwords, O-T-P or two-factor codes, or A-P-I secret keys. Not even with 'support'.

lines.text: Size from your risk budget first. When signals are unclear, NO_TRADE is a real decision.
lines.say: Size from your risk budget first. When signals are unclear, no trade is a real decision.
